task_summary: Extract text from 100+ PDF/DOCX/PPTX files and classify them into 5 subject folders (LLM, trapped_ion_and_qc, black_hole, DNA, music_history) based on content.
decomposition_rationale: The task has two distinct concerns: (1) extracting text from multiple document formats (PDF, DOCX, PPTX) using available libraries and stdlib fallbacks, and (2) classifying documents into 5 predefined categories using keyword matching on extracted text, then moving files. Separating these keeps extraction logic reusable and classification/routing logic independent.

skills.name: evo-document-text-extraction
skills.description: Extracts text from PDF, DOCX, and PPTX files using PyPDF2, pdfplumber, pdftotext CLI, and stdlib zipfile+XML fallbacks. Provides a unified interface that auto-detects file type by extension and returns extracted text. For PDFs, reads only first 2-3 pages for speed. For DOCX/PPTX, uses zipfile+ElementTree since python-docx and python-pptx are not installed.
skills.responsibility: All text extraction from any supported document format. No classification or file movement logic.
dr_sections: 1. PDF Text Extraction Strategies and Implementations
2.2 Fallback: Native Python stdlib Extraction (Zipfile + XML)
3.2 Fallback: Native Python stdlib Extraction (Zipfile + XML)

skills.name: evo-document-classify-and-sort
skills.description: Classifies extracted document text into one of 5 categories (LLM, trapped_ion_and_qc, black_hole, DNA, music_history) using weighted keyword matching, then moves files into the corresponding folders. Uses comprehensive keyword dictionaries tuned to the specific 5 subjects. Handles folder creation, file routing with shutil.move, and ensures every file is placed in exactly one folder.
skills.responsibility: Document classification based on text content, folder creation, and file movement. No text extraction logic.
dr_sections: 5.1 Classification Scope: First Page vs. Full Text
6. Robust File Operations and Folder Management
6.2 The Anatomy of shutil.move() vs shutil.copy2() + os.remove()
